title: Finding evidence before response / Verify the audit access boundary / Separate object and key authority

blocks.text: A GuardDuty finding contains its type, severity, affected resource and suspicious-activity details. Inspect resource identity, activity timestamps and details; preserve the supporting evidence. Follow the established investigation and escalation procedure for that finding type. Severity alone is not a reason for destructive action.

steps.title: Inspect the evidence and the contrast

blocks.text: Record the supplied finding’s type, severity, resource identity and activity timestamps. Keep those activity timestamps rather than replacing them with the time the finding was opened. Preserve the detailed activity evidence and follow the finding-type procedure.

A severe finding adds urgency, not proof of compromise or permission to destroy a resource. If detail is incomplete, preserve what is available and escalate under the established procedure. Missing detail does not establish an attack mechanism.

public.prompt: A supplied GuardDuty finding is severe, but activity details are incomplete. The finding-type procedure says to preserve available evidence and escalate for investigation. Which next step is supported?

options.text: Preserve resource identity, activity timestamps and available finding details, then escalate under that procedure.
Destroy the resource because severity establishes compromise.
Replace the activity timestamps with the time the finding was opened and escalate.

o1.message: The supplied procedure supports preserving evidence and escalation, not a compromise conclusion.

o2.message: Severity alone is not supporting evidence for compromise or destructive action.

o3.message: The investigation must retain the supplied activity timestamps, not the time someone opened the finding.

correct.message: The supplied procedure supports preserving evidence and escalation, not a compromise conclusion.

incorrect.message: Recheck the stated boundary against the evidence; the selected conclusion is not supported.

hints: Identify what the supplied evidence establishes, rather than what a summary might suggest.

public.prompt: Read each triage record against the supplied finding and procedure. Decide whether it meets the evidence-preserving triage criterion. Finding: type=representative suspicious activity; severity=high; resource=node A; activity timestamps=10:00–10:05 UTC; opened=11:00 UTC; detail=unusual activity reported, mechanism not established. Procedure: preserve available finding evidence and escalate for investigation.

items.text: Triage record: type=representative suspicious activity; severity=high; resource=node A; activity=10:00–10:05 UTC; unusual-activity details retained; finding evidence preserved. Next step=escalate for investigation; compromise not asserted; no destructive action.
Triage record: same type, severity and resource; activity=11:00 UTC; details retained; evidence preserved; next step=escalate for investigation. No destructive action.
Triage record: type, severity, resource, activity timestamps and details retained; evidence preserved. Next step=destroy node A because high severity proves compromise.

e1.message: The record retains the affected resource, supplied activity timestamps and supporting details and follows the specified procedure.

e2.message: The record substitutes opening time for the supplied activity timestamps, losing required investigation evidence.

e3.message: Severity alone does not prove compromise or justify destruction; the specified next step is investigation escalation.

blocks.text: S3 bucket policies can grant or deny object operations for specified principals and resource paths. Limit approved audit writers and readers to required actions on intended bucket or object ARNs, and inspect other applicable grants and denies.

Verify the boundary with an approved write, an approved read and an unapproved read. Keep identity and resource path with each result. Encryption or retention settings do not replace these authorization checks.

blocks.takeaway: Check identity, action and resource with each result.

steps.lede: Choose the interpretation supported by the supplied evidence.

public.prompt: An audit bucket has encryption and retention enabled. Which test set verifies the authorization boundary for the intended object path?

options.text: Only inspect encryption and retention settings; no identity tests are needed.
Only test an approved reader; its success establishes that unapproved readers are denied.
An approved writer write, an approved reader read, and an unapproved identity read, recording identity, path and result.

o1.message: Encryption and retention are not authorization checks.

o2.message: Approved read success does not establish the unapproved identity’s result.

o3.message: The three identity-specific tests verify approved access and the denied boundary.

public.prompt: Read each audit authorization review. Decide whether its policy scope and identity-test evidence meet the stated boundary. Approved audit writers require only writing, approved audit readers only reading, on the intended audit object path. Inspect other applicable grants and denies; the approved write/read must succeed and the unapproved read must be denied.

items.text: Review: policy grants every principal read access on the audit path. Approved write/read succeed and the unapproved read succeeds. Encryption and retention enabled; reviewer marks authorization boundary verified.

Review: supplied scoped policy retained. Other applicable grants and denies were not inspected; only the approved read was tested. Encryption enabled; reviewer marks full authorization verification complete.

Review: only the supplied scoped statements apply; all other applicable grants and denies inspected, no broadening. Each test records identity, action, resource and result:

blocks.text: SSE-KMS uses an AWS KMS key; SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys. An SSE-KMS read needs both s3:GetObject permission and kms:Decrypt authority for that key. SSE-S3 does not require KMS key-use permission. Configure the supplied key as bucket default encryption, test approved object/key authority and denied KMS use, and inspect object metadata.

blocks.title: Two encryption models, separate authority boundaries

nodes.label: SSE-S3 object metadata: S3-managed keys; no KMS key-use permission
Bucket default: does not re-encrypt existing objects

blocks.alt_text: Two encryption models, separate authority boundaries. Audit reader; s3:GetObject permission; kms:Decrypt authority for object key; SSE-KMS object metadata; SSE-S3 object metadata: S3-managed keys; no KMS key-use permission; Bucket default: does not re-encrypt existing objects

steps.title: Inspect the evidence and the contrast

blocks.text: For the supplied SSE-KMS object, compare a read with approved s3:GetObject and kms:Decrypt authority against a read with KMS use denied. Inspect that object’s encryption metadata to determine its encryption model.

Changing bucket default encryption does not re-encrypt existing objects. A default setting is therefore not proof of an older object’s encryption. Keep SSE-KMS’s key-use requirement separate from SSE-S3, which needs no KMS key-use permission.

public.prompt: For an object whose metadata confirms SSE-KMS, s3:GetObject is allowed but kms:Decrypt for its key is denied. Which read result is supported?

options.text: The read succeeds because the bucket default was changed to SSE-S3 after this object was stored.
The read fails because both object permission and KMS key-use authority are required.
The read succeeds because s3:GetObject alone is sufficient for SSE-KMS.

o1.message: Changing the bucket default does not re-encrypt existing objects; this object still has SSE-KMS metadata.

o2.message: SSE-KMS reads require both s3:GetObject and kms:Decrypt authority.

o3.message: Object permission does not substitute for KMS key-use authority.

correct.message: SSE-KMS reads require both s3:GetObject and kms:Decrypt authority.

steps.title: Review object and key authority
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which interpretations or proposed actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Read each encryption review and decide whether it correctly verifies both object and key authority. The supplied key is named audit-key; the required default and new object use that key. Existing objects must be judged from their metadata, not from a later bucket-default change.

items.text: Default changed to SSE-S3. Existing object metadata remains SSE-KMS, key=audit-key. Review says the object is now re-encrypted and no longer needs kms:Decrypt.

Default: SSE-KMS, key=audit-key. New object metadata: SSE-KMS, key=audit-key. Read tests: approved s3:GetObject + approved kms:Decrypt -> success; s3:GetObject allowed + KMS use denied -> failure. Review notes: SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys, needs no KMS key-use authority; changing the default does not re-encrypt existing objects.
Default: SSE-KMS, key=audit-key. Object metadata: SSE-KMS, key=audit-key. Review predicts a successful read when s3:GetObject is allowed and KMS use is denied, because object access is sufficient.

e1.message: Changing the bucket default does not re-encrypt this existing SSE-KMS object; its read still requires KMS authority.

e2.message: The default, metadata and contrasting reads verify the supplied key and both required authorities while distinguishing SSE-S3 and existing objects.

e3.message: SSE-KMS reading requires both object permission and KMS key-use authority.
